turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello—what brings you in today? Patient: Honestly, I’m not sure; things just feel off lately. I’ve been making some inappropriate comments and even tried to initiate physical contact with strangers, and I’ve also lost interest in my family.
When did these changes first start, and have they been gradually worsening or did they appear suddenly?
They started about six months ago and, if anything, they’ve been gradually getting worse—people keep noticing it more. I don’t really notice a clear “sudden” moment myself.
To help narrow this down, could you please tell me your age?

Have you or your family noticed any changes in your memory, language, or ability to handle daily tasks like managing finances or organizing your schedule, or has the change been primarily limited to your behavior and personality?

“I guess my memory and daily tasks aren’t really the biggest issue—I’ve mostly just felt apathetic and kind of checked out from family, and I’ve been making odd, inappropriate comments. I haven’t been managing my routine as well lately, but it feels more like loss of interest than forgetting.”
Have you noticed any changes in your eating habits, such as a strong craving for sweets or overeating, or have you developed any new repetitive behaviors or rituals?

I’ve developed a real craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, and I’ve been eating more than I used to. I haven’t really noticed any specific rituals, but I do feel more drawn to those foods and it’s hard to ignore. Also, I’ve gained about 10 kilograms over this period.
Do you have any family history of early-onset dementia, neurological disorders, or psychiatric conditions?

“I don’t know of any early dementia in my family, and I haven’t been told of major neurological problems. I’m not sure about psychiatric history either—I usually avoid getting into details, but nothing specific comes to mind.”
To rule out structural or acute neurological causes, have you experienced any recent headaches, vision changes, weakness, numbness, or difficulty with speech or balance?

“I haven’t had headaches or vision changes, and I’m not noticing weakness, numbness, or trouble with speech or balance. I mostly feel apathetic and socially off, like I’m checked out, but I don’t feel physically unwell.”
[DDX] Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, Frontal lobe neoplasm, Late-onset bipolar disorder, Alzheimer disease, Vascular dementia
